Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon. Stock in NVIDIA failed today after
the computer chip maker stepped CEO stepped down. But as NPR's Scott Horsley reports,
the broader market also lost a little ground. A sudden departure of CEO Jensen Wong as a blow
for NVIDIA. Wong co-founded the company and steered its meteoric rise as a leading designer
of semiconductors prized by the booming artificial intelligence business. Wong abruptly resigned after
acknowledging having an affair with a woman who's suspected of spying for China. NVIDIA did not have
a succession plan in place before the news broke two weeks ago. Chief Financial Officer Collette
Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor can be found. NVIDIA shares have dropped
around 30 percent from their peak last month, reflecting not only the suspected spy scandal,
but also wider jitters about the staying power of the AI boom. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Jensen Wong had a close working relationship with President Trump. But as Kara Swisher told NPR's
Here Now, many questions remain over whether Wong's actions pose any security concerns.
There's a lot going on here with national security, especially what did the Trump
administration know and when did they know it? Of course, Trump has pretended he didn't know
much or Jensen didn't know much. And there's a lot of questions as to why the government didn't
tell Jensen Wong this was going on. Apparently they didn't, apparently, but we'll see.
NVIDIA's interim leader, Collette Kress, says she will build on NVIDIA's foundation
and continue the company's leadership in accelerating computing and AI.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says there are new speed restrictions affecting
Star Shield, the military version of the Starlink satellite service the Ukrainian military uses on
the front lines. NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports. Zelensky warned the restrictions are helping Russia
carry out more accurate attacks and causing further Ukrainian casualties. He said the
restrictions have affected Ukrainian military operations for several days across the entire
front line and that the speed restrictions that kick in at 100 miles an hour make it more difficult
to intercept Russia's new jet powered drones. Zelensky said the speed restrictions are not
due to random technical errors but are systematic. They come just as the U.S. is again pushing
negotiations to try to end the war. Star Shield was first restricted three weeks ago as President
Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia. Then it was reinstated. Owner Elon Musk admitted he
was behind slowing Starlink previously but claimed the U.S. government controls access to Star Shield.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Kyiv. President Donald Trump has urged Vice President J.D. Vance
to shift focus from the Iran war to tackling corruption and crime in democratic controlled
areas. On social media, the president posted, "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days
have long since passed." You're listening to NPR.
Broadway's spring season is going to be filled with Hollywood stars from Julia Roberts to Jessica
Chastain to Steve Carell. Reporter Jeff London says the big ticket celebrities are coming with
big ticket prices. Steve Carell and John C. Reilly will star in a revival of Neil Simon's The Odd
Couple and Jessica Chastain will star in a new play about an actress with dementia. Also opening
this spring is Julie Roberts with Paul Rudd in Small Mouth Sounds, a comic and touching play where
hardly anyone speaks. These productions will be open for limited runs and given the limited
supply of seats available, ticket prices are high. If you want to see Julia Roberts from the best
seats, be prepared to fork out almost $650. For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
Lawmakers in Spain have ratified new housing measures aimed at limiting evictions and real
estate speculation. The measures come just one day after a general strike and major protests
over the high cost of housing in Spain. Since the new rules were passed by Spain's interim
lower house of parliament, they could be revised depending upon the outcome of this month's
general election. That's because the conservative popular party has vowed to repeal the housing
